content: The Group 3 elements are chemical elements that occupy the third vertical column of the periodic table. The International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC) has not established a definitive format for the periodic table, allowing for variations in how Group 3 is represented. The elements scandium (Sc) and yttrium (Y) are universally recognized as members of Group 3. However, the classification of the remaining elements in this group varies depending on the convention used. 1. Some periodic tables include lanthanum (La) and actinium (Ac) as the additional members of Group 3. These elements are the starting points of the lanthanide and actinide series, respectively. In their most common tripositive ionic forms, these elements lack partially filled f orbitals, which gives them chemical behavior more similar to d-block elements. 2. Other periodic tables include lutetium (Lu) and lawrencium (Lr) as the remaining members of Group 3. These elements mark the end of the lanthanide and actinide series, respectively. In their ground-state electron configurations, the f-shell is nominally full, making them behave more like d-block metals compared to other lanthanides and actinides. This similarity in properties aligns them more closely with scandium and yttrium. For lawrencium, this behavior is theoretically expected but has not been experimentally observed due to the lack of sufficient quantities of the element. 3. A third alternative is to include all 30 lanthanide and actinide elements in Group 3. Lanthanides, as electropositive trivalent metals, share closely related chemistry and exhibit many similarities to scandium and yttrium. 4. A fourth alternative excludes all lanthanides and actinides from Group 3. This approach is based on the fact that lanthanides possess unique properties due to their partially filled f orbitals, which are not shared by scandium and yttrium. Additionally, actinides display a much broader range of chemical behaviors, such as varying oxidation states, making comparisons to scandium and yttrium even less relevant. Scandium, yttrium, and the lanthanides (excluding promethium) are often found together in the Earth's crust. They are relatively abundant compared to most d-block metals but are typically more challenging to extract from their ores. From a biological perspective, Group 3 elements are generally hard metals with low solubility in aqueous environments, resulting in limited availability to the biosphere. None of the Group 3 elements have any known biological role in living organisms. The radioactivity of actinides makes them particularly toxic to living cells.
